messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: p0 serving-runtime alerts — multiple CUDA OOMs + container crashloop in eu-west-1. Autoscaler showing rapid scale up/down. Paging oncall (jamie). Please ack and triage.

jamie: acked. I’m on it. seeing a spike of OOMs + kubelet OOM-kill on pods serving gpu-models. Affected pool: gpu-prod-eu-1.

mike: I’m pulling logs from the runtime pods now. Initial suspicion: rapid pod churn causing KV cache thrash -> higher memory + OOMs. Also seeing driver resets in dmesg.

lina: I can see CA (cluster-autoscaler) activity: nodes being provisioned then marked NotReady then drained. Autoscaler config shows scale-down aggressive (scaleDownUtilizationThreshold=0.2) — might be too permissive for this workload.

ashley: also noticed a recent deploy (deploy-bot) 30m ago for a v2 scheduler tweak that increased pod replica targets for some routes. Could be increasing burst demand. Reverting that would reduce churn.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-11-02T13:12:23Z: scheduler/v2 change rolled to prod (rollout-id cf9a).

jamie: mitigation plan: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler scale-ups/scale-downs 2) cordon suspect nodes 3) set HPA min to current + keep stable 4) route a % of traffic to standby region. Doing step 1 now.

mike: commands to pause CA quickly: 

```
kubectl -n kube-system edit deployment cluster-autoscaler
# set spec.replicas=0 or add annotation autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true
```

mike: I recommend setting replicas=0 temporarily — will stop both scale up and down. Lina, can you cordon the noisy nodes?

lina: cordoning nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7a` and `kubectl cordon gpu-node-9b`. Also adding taint `taint nodes gpu-node-* gpu-thrash=true:NoSchedule` to prevent new pods. Doing now.

jamie: done pausing CA (replicas=0). Confirmed no new node launches in the past 30s.

ashley: rolling back scheduler tweak to reduce replica targets. Triggering rollback of rollout cf9a to previous stable.

mike: I pulled a pod log excerpt (truncated):

```
2024-11-02T13:35:12Z runtime ERROR cuda: out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB
2024-11-02T13:35:13Z runtime WARN kv_cache: eviction spike, cache miss rate 78%
2024-11-02T13:35:14Z kernel: Killed process 24321 (runtime) total-vm:1024000kB, anon-rss:900000kB
```

mike: also checked GPU driver: `nvidia-smi` on affected node shows GPU reset count increment and ECC memory errors on GPU0. That suggests hardware/driver instability under rapid churn.

sara: customer-facing: we have elevated error rates on hosted API for some EU customers. Starting a notification draft for SRE/CS to evaluate impacted tenants. Keep me posted on severity and estimated time to restore.

jamie: quick fallback: switching traffic for heavy-generation routes to a quantized/cpu-friendly variant to reduce GPU pressure. Updating route policy in gateway to reroute 20% initially.

mike: applying a temporary model variant weight in routing: `gateway set-weight route=generate-prod variant=gptq-7b 20%`. Also scaling down GPU replicas for low-priority routes: `kubectl scale deploy/serve-lowprio --replicas=1`.

lina: after cordon + pause CA, crashloops stopped on cordoned nodes but pods are evicting onto remaining nodes and some still OOM. I recommend we create a small dedicated nodepool with instances that have larger GPU memory (A100-40GB) and schedule critical pods there. Creating nodepool now.

ashley: provisioning standby nodepool (gpu-large-eu-temp) with 3 A100-40 nodes. Will add nodeSelector `node.kubernetes.io/size=large-temp` to critical deployments.

jamie: handoff — I need to step out in 15m. Mike, you take primary on-call from here for mitigation and root-cause. Lina to continue node operations, Ashley to manage infra changes, Sara on customer comms.

mike: taking over. I’ll: 1) verify standby nodepool accepts pods 2) migrate critical replicas there 3) monitor OOM and driver resets 4) prepare rollback for rollout if needed.

mike: migrating critical pods: `kubectl patch deploy serve-critical -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"nodeSelector": {"node.kubernetes.io/size":"large-temp"}}}}}'`

mike: immediate observation: pods scheduled to large-temp nodes are stable, no OOMs after 2 minutes. GPU driver resets stopped on those nodes. Suggest we keep CA paused and keep traffic split until we confirm stability for 10m.

lina: created incident tag and added runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving-runtime-oom. Also taking heap snapshots and collecting node dmesg and driver logs for postmortem.

sara: drafted customer note: "We experienced elevated error rates for some EU inference requests starting at 13:30 UTC due to GPU node instability during autoscaling. We have mitigations in place and traffic has been partially routed to a stable pool. We expect full recovery within the hour. We will provide postmortem with root cause and remediation." Sharing with CS for review.

deploy-bot: rollback started: rollout cf9a -> previous stable at 13:48 UTC.

mike: monitoring metrics: error rate down 70%, latency returning to normal. No new OOMs on large-temp nodes. Proposing follow-up actions before we unpause CA: 1) reduce CA aggressiveness (increase scaleDownUtilizationThreshold) 2) add stabilizationWindow to HPA/CA 3) improve model-scheduler coordination to avoid large simultaneous replica changes 4) hardware health checks for nodes with frequent GPU resets.

jamie: thanks all. I’m handing off fully to mike. I’ll be reachable via DM.

mike: ack. I’ll keep this thread updated and raise a postmortem ticket once we stabilize. Preliminary severity: P1; customer impact: elevated errors for a subset of EU traffic (10-15% of requests to generation endpoints) for ~30-40m.

lina: collecting artifacts now: kube events, pod logs, node dmesg, cluster-autoscaler activity logs. Will attach to postmortem.

ashley: infra follow-ups I’ll own: node labeling for migration, CA config change proposal, and a temporary autoscaler kill-switch documented in runbooks.

sara: CS will send the initial customer note in 10m and update with ETA.

oncall-bot: NOTE: jamie handed off oncall to mike at 13:55 UTC.

mike: final for now — keeping CA paused and traffic split. Will reopen CA only after we confirm 15m steady state. If anyone sees regression ping me directly.

sara: thanks everyone. Adding this to postmortem queue and assigning owners for actions.

mike: end of thread update at 14:07 UTC — continuing monitoring.
